blocks.x: The contract behind Patient Priority Portal — Industry Use Cases: signed baseline in week two, working slice by week eight, industrialized controls by week twelve, and evidence flowing to your control owner throughout.

blocks.title: Patient Priority Portal — reference flow in production
blocks.note: Contracts between stages are enforced at the boundary, so schema drift fails loudly in minutes instead of quietly in a quarter.

blocks.x: The build sequence is deliberate: contracts and identity first, the working decision slice second, the verification harness third — because a Patient Priority Portal — Industry Use Cases capability without its eval gate is just another unattended automation.

items: Diagnose (2-4 weeks)
Baseline measured and signed, the metric and owner named, the risk envelope agreed in writing.
Prove (6-10 weeks)
The pilot runs on real data with a control group — the gate review happens whether the news is good or not.
Industrialize (1-3 quarters)
Hardening, enablement and scale-out in that order — no rollout faster than the evidence.
Compound (ongoing)
The next decisions enter the same loop — the backlog ranked by measured value per week of effort.

blocks.x: Runbooks stop being tribal knowledge: the platform records the operating narrative as it happens, and new team members inherit a system, not a legend.

The integration pattern for Patient Priority Portal — Industry Use Cases is read-first and contract-first: integrate to the system of record without copying it, and let typed contracts govern what crosses the boundary.

blocks.x: We run Patient Priority Portal — Industry Use Cases in gates: each one reviews measured deltas against the signed baseline with your named owners in the room, and each one can stop the program. That is the discipline most enterprise programs are missing.
